title: Connect frozen fixed-tick oracles to public device runners
requires: Host able to build and execute the public conformance runner
scope: Repair the final F8 qualification harness exposed by F8-28: execute the already-frozen realtime-single-step-v1 oracle suite through normal public API creation and stepping on each selected production driver. Do not change physics, fixed work budgets, advertised capabilities, tolerances, realtime-candidate-v4, or the legacy variable-timestep profiles. This is qualification integration only; driver-private state cannot satisfy an assertion.
acceptance: A backend-neutral public runner executes every applicable frozen runtime adapter, domain, coupling, lifecycle, negative-control and scenario row with exactly one dt=1/60 step, one spatial publication and the fixed dispatch/iteration/synchronization budget per tick.

Independent public-output assertions cover all twelve frozen scenario fixtures, including cold start, sustained execution, impact, rotation, stiff systems, mass ratio, containment, source/removal/replacement, overflow recovery, empty and sparse capacity.

The runner emits reviewable observation artifacts accepted by realtime_oracle.py and identifies the exact candidate manifest, runtime variant, binary, device and toolchain without reading driver-private state.

Legacy variable-timestep quality profiles and their historical evidence remain unchanged. The qualification report explicitly distinguishes those historical profiles from the sole fixed-tick oracle instead of submitting invalid pre-F8 steps or relabeling measurements.

Portable deterministic tests cover successful observations, missing rows, wrong timestep/substep, extra catch-up steps, changed work budgets, unsupported advertised rows and failed execution; the same runner is usable by CPU, CUDA, Vulkan, D3D12 and Metal qualification tasks.
